status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: The NPC architecture, archetypes, cast, factions, standing, culture data and the consultation plan.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

factions.name: New France (troops, Canadien militia and traders)
The town (campaign's community)
factions.note: Each town is its own community with its own standing.

factions.name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy (Six Nations)
factions.note: Officially neutral in the war until the 1759 Niagara campaign; member nations and towns chose differently.

factions.name: Kanonwalohale (Oneida)
factions.note: The Oneida town the playable town is modelled on; its in-game name is set with the nation (20.9). Kirkland's mission from 1766 (N:4).

factions.name: Canajoharie (Mohawk upper castle)
factions.note: Hendrick Theyanoguin's town; the George Klock deed disputes; a Mohawk town surrounded by settlers, where settlers' stock in the corn was a standing grievance. Molly Brant's store opened here after July 1774.

factions.name: Tiononderoge (Mohawk lower castle)
factions.note: Beside Fort Hunter and its Anglican chapel (since 1712).

factions.name: Oquaga (Susquehanna, many nations)
factions.note: A multi-nation town on the upper Susquehanna with a mission from the 1750s; Lenape and Munsee families live and visit here.

factions.name: Kahnawake
factions.note: Mission community near Montreal, allied to New France until 1760; its carriers and traders worked the Albany-Montreal trade (E:S25).

factions.name: Akwesasne
factions.note: Founded about 1755 by families from Kahnawake.

factions.name: Oswegatchie (La Présentation)
factions.note: The Sulpician mission of 1749 that drew Onondaga, Oneida and Cayuga families to the French side.

factions.name: Schaghticoke
factions.note: A Hudson valley refuge community; many of its people had moved north to Missisquoi and Saint-François by the 1750s.

factions.name: Stockbridge (Mohican)
factions.note: A mission town in western Massachusetts; its men served in ranger companies (N:18).

alignments_by_era.note: Era-level alignments for hostility rolls, by nation and by community. Real towns and people chose differently; review with historians and nations before shipping. Hostility comes only from alignment, the war state and reputation, never from ethnicity.

era.war_1755_1758.notes: The Confederacy was officially neutral; Mohawk towns fought with Johnson; Mississauga, Odawa and Ojibwe were at Oswego in 1756 and Fort William Henry in 1757; Ohio Lenape and Shawnee raided the Pennsylvania and Virginia frontier until Easton (October 1758) [H] (N:9, N:11, N:19).

era.war_1759_1760.notes: The Confederacy joined the Niagara campaign in 1759; the Canadian mission communities made peace at Oswegatchie and Kahnawake in 1760 [H] (N:9, N:11).

era.tense_peace_1761_1762.tension: gift and powder cuts; a Seneca war belt in 1761 (N:15)

era.war_1763_1764.notes: Pontiac's War. Genesee Seneca fought (Devil's Hole, 1763); Johnson kept most of the Six Nations out and in 1764 sent Mohawk and Oneida parties against Susquehanna Lenape towns [H] (N:15, N:21).

era.line_1768_1773.tension: the Fort Stanwix line and its cession of Shawnee and Lenape hunting grounds; the Stump murders (1768); squatters beyond the line (E:S33, N:17)

era.dunmore_1774.tension: Yellow Creek (April 1774) and Dunmore's War at the Ohio node (N:14)

standing.visit: One visit per community per game day: leaving and re-entering the same day is the same visit.

fair_trade.per: visit with 120 d or more traded

share_game.poached_meat: meat taken on the recipients' own grounds without leave counts for nothing

merry_company.per: visit (cond.drunk merry, taverns and garrison only)

standing.ceilings: Standing above 50 (Trusted) can be reached only through earned sources: jobs, honoured debts, councils attended, obligations kept and time. Gifts, sharing and company alone reach Friendly at most (review 2, issue 4).
standing.gossip: Every community remembers, settler and Native alike: cheating or theft found out spreads to the whole community in a game day and to its neighbours at half strength (review 1, issue 21).
standing.wartime_alignment: set by player choices (enlisting, scouting, trading with the other side)

effects.hostile: attack on sight in war; refuse trade in peace
effects.friendly: credit, some teaching, lodging for a price
effects.trusted: most teaching, free lodging, invitations to councils and the household's round

kinship.rule: Adoption or kinship is never a reward for standing. It is a scripted, consented event that can follow specific circumstances: a condolence after a death in a household the player stood by, a rescue or captivity story, or a political alliance the council chooses. The household decides; the player may decline; the script is reviewed with the nation (review 1, issue 8).

worship.note: Christian services, seen from outside; never a mechanic

observance.note: Private: NPCs are indoors or away and not interactable; nothing is shown.

away.note: Record tier only: the NPC is off the map (hunting, campaign, trade trip).

archetypes.name: Half-pay officer or hired scout
archetypes.notes: Winter scouts on snowshoes (K:2). Ranger and provincial companies included Stockbridge Mohican and Mohegan men and free Black men (N:18, N:10).
archetypes.v3_note: Id kept from v2. In 1765 the ranging companies are disbanded: this archetype is a half-pay officer or a local woodsman the post hires as a scout or express rider (review 1 of v2, blocker). In the 1757 and 1761 starts ('post') it is a ranger again.

season:winter.note: mill idle when the race freezes: craft at home

archetypes.name: Household member (valley)
archetypes.notes: Any member of a valley household, free or enslaved. People are never property in any mechanic.

archetypes.name: Pastor (German Reformed or Lutheran) or missionary
Senior woman of a clan household
archetypes.notes: Senior women held the fields and food stores and had a voice in councils and in choosing leaders (E:S44, N:7). She decides food sales and speaks on the town's rum policy.

archetypes.name: Hunter
archetypes.notes: The Haudenosaunee pattern: a mainly male fall hunt from October, home for Midwinter, spring fishing and sugaring; men build houses and clear land (N:6, N:7). Pelts return for the spring trade (record tier).

archetypes.name: Field worker and skin dresser
archetypes.notes: Women worked the fields collectively under senior women (E:S44).

archetypes.name: Healer
archetypes.notes: Preparations were kept private (K:8): some knowledge is never for sale. Ceremony is not a game mechanic.

archetypes.name: Elder
archetypes.v3_note: The elder's expertise is local history, land cases, the hunting grounds and diplomacy. By 1765 Oneida households struck fire with flint and steel like everyone else; friction fire is learned from a backcountry hunter, a book or experiment, and no fire-drill content touches ceremony without consultation (review 1 of v2, minor 14).

archetypes.name: Missionary or schoolmaster at the town
archetypes.notes: Present from 1766 (modelled on Kirkland's mission, N:4). Christian and traditional practice exist side by side in the town; the missionary is one voice among many and has no authority in the council.

archetypes.name: Lenape or Munsee visitor
archetypes.notes: Families from the upper Susquehanna (Oquaga, Wyoming) visiting kin and council. The Walking Purchase is their grievance and theirs to tell.

archetypes.name: Trader of a nation's trading party
archetypes.notes: Kahnawake carriers on the Albany-Montreal route, Oneida and Onondaga parties bound for Oswego, Mohawk traders from Canajoharie. They compare markets and sell where it pays.

archetypes.name: Long hunter (Virginia and Carolina)
archetypes.notes: Only at the Ohio node after 1761: hunters from southwest Virginia and western North Carolina ranging into Kentucky and Tennessee (N:24).

archetypes.name: Delegates travelling to council
archetypes.notes: Delegations on their way to councils at Johnson Hall, Onondaga or the Carry.

archetypes.name: Patrol or armed party
archetypes.notes: Composition follows the war state and alignment of named communities: regulars, provincials, rangers, Canadien militia, warriors of an allied community. There is no ethnic 'hostile' type; peace-time parties are travellers.

individuals.notes: Enslaved people were a sizeable share of Albany and Mohawk valley households (review 1, issue 15). They speak in their own voice, have their own aims and relationships, and no mechanic treats anyone as property. The script is written and reviewed with a sensitivity reader before this row ships.
individuals.sensitivity_context: For the sensitivity reviewer: New York's 1712 act made manumission very hard: an owner freeing a person had to post a 200-pound security and pay the freed person a 20-pound annuity (N:40; verify the text in the colonial laws). Tobias's aim to buy his family's freedom therefore runs into the law as well as money, and the script should show that. Most Black New Yorkers in 1765 were enslaved; free Black property holders were rare.

culture_data.rule: Native NPCs use the same needs, schedule and economy systems as everyone; nation and town culture data layers on top (Y:9.5). Names, dwellings, food names, seasonal rounds and town layouts are drafted here from the scholarship and signed off with the nation before the town milestone.

portrayal_rules: Use nation and community names in the UI and narration. Colonial characters may use period terms in their own speech, reviewed with the nation's office.
Native NPCs are producers, consumers, diplomats and neighbours who host, refuse, negotiate and remember.
Show women's authority over fields, food and (among the Haudenosaunee) leadership choices.
Ceremonies (Midwinter, the harvest observance, councils' ritual) are calendar events or invitations, never playable spectacle or crafts.
No scalping or scalp bounties as mechanics; wampum is diplomacy, not money; no sacred items as loot.
Conflict has causes on every side: land fraud, broken promises, gift and powder cuts, encroachment, retaliation.

consultation.rule: Each nation's content is reviewed by that nation's offices; content ships only after its own sign-off. The live slice (M1-M2) depicts no Native people. First contact is now, before any further Native content is drafted; existing drafts in this backlog go to the offices as a starting point, marked not final.

release_rule: Names ship for everyone at once after consultation. Every named or role-titled NPC carries a persona of the same depth (family, opinions, life lines).
